This, Amazon says, is the “symphony of people and technology” to which the retail giant owes its success. Following a barrage of negative publicity about working practices, Amazon began to open up its fulfilment centres to carefully controlled free public tours a decade ago. item.title: AI is imposing a hidden ‘cognitive tax’ on the lowest-paid workers
item.description: It’s time to rethink welfare as AI reshapes the economy and wears down the brains of some of the most vulnerable workers AI is adding to the cognitive load of workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt – and the lowest paid feel it most. We need to rethink welfare for an economy being reshaped by AI. Throughout the history of the study of economics, the human brain, which directs our labour, judgment and resilience, has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that. As machines take on routine work, what becomes most valuable is the judgment, creativity and insights only people can provide. Economists coined a term for this in recent years: brain capital. Professor Dame Henrietta Moore is founder and director of the UCL Institute for Global Prosperity and co-leads The New Alignment, the institute’s G20 policy programme Continue reading...

item.title: Parents: please don’t buy Grand Theft Auto VI for your child
item.description: Rockstar Games’ brilliant 18-rated criminal caper is stuffed with sex, drugs and violence. It is the most explicit game I’ve ever played – and it really is not for kids Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI? I am haunted still by an interaction I had at my stepson’s ninth birthday party in 2014, where one of the kids asked if I could put on Grand Theft Auto V for them all. “I have it at home!”, he said, giving me the puppy-dog eyes. Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “ no way” . Later I gently mentioned to the kid’s mother that GTA V was an 18-rated game and really wasn’t suitable for kids. “Oh, but he’s really good at these games,” she told me.
